rules.title: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance: source-of-income discrimination prohibited
rules.requirement: Landlords and rental agents in Cambridge may not refuse to rent to you, or set different terms, because of your source of income, including a Section 8 voucher or public benefits. If this happens, you can file a complaint with the Cambridge Human Rights Commission (617-349-4396).

coverage.summary: Covers rental housing transactions in Cambridge, except two-family dwellings where the owner lives in the building.

rules.exemptions: Exemption for 2-family dwellings when the owner lives there. Landlords may still apply reasonable standards uniformly, such as ability to pay rent and to care for the apartment.
rules.penalty: After a hearing, the Commission may file a criminal complaint in District Court, levy civil fines of up to $300 for each violation, seek injunctive relief in Superior Court, and seek damages, expenses and other relief.
rules.citation: Cambridge Municipal Code ch. 14.04 (Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance)
rules.quoted_span: Source of Income, includes Section 8 and public benefits

notes: The document is an official Human Rights Commission web page summarizing the Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance (ch. 14.04). The source-of-income protected category appears only as a list item, and the page states the ordinance prohibits discrimination in renting. No section number, effective date or criminal-history rule is given. The $300 fine is described generally for Commission remedies.
